name: Motorcycle
description: A road-registered motor vehicle with a seat and no more than three wheels, including a motor scooter, that isn't a low-speed electric bicycle or a motorized bicycle. An electric two- or three-wheeler that can go faster than 39 mph without pedaling is one, whatever its power.

restrictions.rule: A saddle or seat, and no more than three wheels on the ground; includes motor scooters, and excludes autocycles
Can go faster than 39 mph on level ground without pedaling, above what a motorized bicycle may; there is no power threshold
Riders need a Class M license or motorcycle endorsement, earned by passing the knowledge, skills and vision tests; an approved motorcycle course waives the skills test
A rider under 18 must complete an approved motorcycle education course before a Class M license is issued
A rider on a motorcycle instruction permit must be accompanied by a licensed rider on a separate vehicle within sight and hearing
Titled and registered with the county treasurer for $20 a year ($10 once it is more than five model years old), plus a $9 annual electric motorcycle fee for a battery-electric one
Must carry financial liability coverage, with proof on board, to be driven on a highway
Carries a passenger only if it is designed for one, with passenger footrests
A 1977 or later model must keep a headlamp lit on the highway
No more than two abreast in a lane, and no riding between lanes or rows of traffic
Any motorcycle may also be registered with the DNR as an all-terrain vehicle, and one with design features for natural terrain counts as an off-road motorcycle
